question: Can a semantic cache reuse a yes/no answer after a policy or question polarity changes?
memory: Each repetition replaces eight tenant-a embeddings and checks 128 semantic scores against current vectors. Deleting tenant a leaves eight tenant-b records unchanged by live equality assertion and matching full-document hashes.
scoreScale: MongoDB score=(1+cosine)/2; PostgreSQL control reports cosine.
modelRoleCaveat: Stored cache questions use document instruction; lookup questions use query instruction. Higher-threshold misses are specific to this asymmetric configuration. Symmetric cache embeddings were not tested.
methodTiming: Cases, labels and thresholds frozen locally before inference. Index-score validation was added after embedding observations but before any database execution. No public preregistration or universal threshold recommendation.
scope: Official MongoDB cache/store adapters; PostgreSQL is an exact-vector control, not a competing semantic-cache implementation.
limitations: Authored fictional policies and YES/NO cache fixtures, not generated answers or representative traffic.
Two repeats of the same frozen model outputs/cases are not independent corpora.
Namespaced privileged fixtures, not production identity authorization.
Search-index data uses a bounded RAM filesystem; no index durability or platform performance/cost result.
Full neighboring-document equality is asserted in the live worker; raw neighboring documents are not independently reconstructed by the audit.
